questions.question: What invariant should a production multimodal system preserve across preprocessing, fusion, and output?
options: Every modality must use the same encoder
Claims remain traceable to transformed source evidence, and missing or conflicting evidence stays visible
The model must always accept every uploaded file
All modalities must receive an equal token budget
questions.explanation: Traceability and explicit evidence limits prevent a fluent output from implying that unavailable, discarded, or contradictory media was verified.

questions.question: An invoice workflow needs to validate a printed total against purchase-order data. Which route is the strongest starting point?
options: Text only, because structured fields are always correct
Vision only, because images contain all business context
Vision plus text or record evidence, fused as typed claims with deterministic validation
Video plus audio, because more modalities always improve quality
questions.explanation: The visual document and authoritative record answer different parts of the task. Evidence-level fusion keeps their claims inspectable before a financial action.

questions.question: Why can uniformly sampled video frames fail even when every selected frame is analyzed correctly?
options: Sampling can omit the short event needed to answer the question
Video frames cannot be represented as visual tokens
Uniform sampling always increases audio quality
Temporal order no longer matters after encoding
questions.explanation: Temporal coverage is part of the evidence contract. A correct analysis of incomplete samples can still miss the decisive event.

questions.question: OCR reports an invoice total with 96% confidence, but the rendered page and purchase order agree on a different amount. What should happen before payment?
options: Pay the OCR amount because its confidence is highest
Average the two numeric totals
Preserve the disagreement and route the high-impact action to validation or human review
Drop the lower-confidence modalities from the trace
questions.explanation: Model confidence is not correctness, and cross-modal disagreement is operational evidence. A high-impact action should fail closed until the conflict is resolved.

questions.question: When is a cheap-first cascade preferable to sending every modality through one large joint model?
options: When a bounded first stage can safely decide that richer media processing is unnecessary
Whenever the task includes an image
When provenance is not required
Only when all requests are processed offline
questions.explanation: A cascade saves cost and latency when its gate is safe and measurable. It must not suppress evidence required by the product contract.

questions.question: Which evaluation suite best supports a multimodal release decision?
options: One aggregate accuracy score from clean inputs
Only average API latency
Task success and grounding by modality slice, conflict handling, missing-evidence behavior, p95 latency, cost, and privacy checks
A list of supported file extensions
questions.explanation: A production suite must test quality and system behavior across the media transformations, disagreement states, and operating constraints the product will encounter.
